facility_desc: 855,000 sf robotics fulfillment center, NW Swigert Way (Trammell Crow developer; Columbia Cascade Enterprise Zone)
program: Oregon Enterprise Zone property tax exemption (ORS 285C.175), Columbia Cascade EZ (Fairview/Troutdale)
issuer: City of Troutdale: Resolution 2377 and council minutes of 2017-05-23 (Columbia Cascade Enterprise Zone sponsor)
notes: Primary: Troutdale City Council minutes 2017-05-23 (saved, agenda packet record 5400665) record Finance Director Erich Mueller estimating about 9.6M of tax abated over the 5-year extended exemption (abatement years from 2019), about 7.2M net of the 25% community service fee, on a 178.4M investment (855,000 sf robotics fulfillment center, TRIP lots 6-8, about 74 acres); the application states 1,050 full-time jobs (city expected about double). Resolution 2377 passed 7-0 (resolution PDF saved; it is a scanned image with no text layer, not OCRed because the minutes carry the same terms). Value is the city's estimate, not a payout. The state's realized figures for the same zone are in the separate realized row; do not add the two. The Oregonian (2022-12-18) also says local officials promised about 10M. Earlier note kept: Tax Fairness Oregon 2019 testimony (HB 2053) says Business Oregon told legislators of a Regionally Significant Industrial Site agreement for the Troutdale facility and one in Hillsboro; the data.oregon.gov RSIS award list (FY2020-FY2026) names no Amazon project (Port of Portland TRIP Phase 2, FY2026, 16.6M, is area infrastructure, not an Amazon award). Site match: Swigert Way = PDX9 1250 NW Swigert Way.

program: Oregon Enterprise Zone property tax exemption (ORS 285C), 5-year extended abatement, as reported by the state (Part A, Enterprise Zone Business Projects)
issuer: Oregon Business Oregon / Department of Revenue Enterprise Zone report, published on data.oregon.gov (taxpayer shown as Amazon.com dedc LLC)
notes: Sum of property_taxes_abated for tax years 2019-20 to 2025-26 for the Columbia Cascade rows: 515,073 + 2,637,465 + 2,741,569 + 2,818,515 + 2,496,763 + 147,500 + 114,739 = 11,471,624. These are taxes abated (gross); under the Troutdale agreement 25% of abated tax is returned as a community service fee, so net to Amazon is about 75% (not computed here). Exemption tranches began 2019, 2020 and 2021 (cost of qualified property 362.8M in 2022-24 reports). Reported jobs 3,051 to 3,862 exceed the 1,050 promised for PDX9, so the zone entry probably also covers other Amazon property (Fairview DPD7 is inside Columbia Cascade EZ); site split not possible from the state file. Part C 2026 shows two tranches now taxable. Lower-bound caveat: portal files start with the 2019-20 report. Overlaps the Troutdale estimated_value row; do not add.

facility_desc: Amazon.com dedc LLC project in Portland Enterprise Zone (candidates PDX6/HPD1 15000 N Lombard St, Schmeer Rd sites DPD2/SOR3/EUG5, UOR2)
program: Oregon Enterprise Zone property tax exemption, Portland E-Zone (Prosper Portland written agreement), 5-year, as reported by the state (Part A)
issuer: Oregon Business Oregon / Department of Revenue Enterprise Zone report, published on data.oregon.gov (taxpayer shown as Amazon.com dedc LLC p)
notes: Sum of property_taxes_abated: 845,472 (2020-21) + 938,690 (2021-22) + 934,822 (2022-23) + 927,501 (2023-24) + 954,512 (2024-25) + 5,016 (2025-26) = 4,606,013. The 143,976,000 investment is the cumulative cost of qualified property in the 2023-25 reports; tranches began 2020, 2021 and 2022; reported jobs 224 to 445 (300 in 2024-26). Part C 2026 lists the 2020 tranches as now taxable. The state file gives no street address, so the Portland facility is unresolved. Corroboration: The Oregonian (2022-12-18, saved) says Portland awarded Amazon and other warehouse firms tax breaks worth more than 1.4M the previous year, and that Amazon saved more than 15M in property taxes on Portland-area and Salem warehouses 2019-2022 (the state rows for Troutdale, Hillsboro, Portland and Salem through 2021-22 sum to about 14.8M). The 2023 state law (HB 2009) bars new retail fulfillment centers from enterprise zones; existing agreements continue.

Hillsboro's 2019 letter to the Senate Workforce Committee (saved) says Amazon had more than 800 part-time jobs besides full-time jobs and that the city charges a community service fee to abated firms.
